newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK NBS TO DISCUSS REPO RATE SITUATION.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK NBS TO DISCUSS REPO RATE SITUATION.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Wednesday said it would discuss whether or not to change its repo rate, currently 9.7 percent, after a rise in the average yield at a Finance Ministry 40-week T-bill auction.
"We still need to discuss our possible reaction to that, therefore any advanced comments would be only pure speculation at the moment," Peter Andresic, NBS chief dealer, told Reuters.
Average yield at the Finance Ministry 40-week T-bill auction hit 10.12 percent, up from 9.986 percent in the last auction of bills with similar maturity -- 39-week T-bills -- on November 14.
"It was an increase in absolute numbers, but less relatively, if we compare both figures," Andresic said.
"The ministry accepted almost everything offered by the banks," he added.
The finance ministry accepted 3.97 billion crowns worth of bids out of total bids of 4.27 billion crowns.
Dealers said they expected Wednesday's yield would bring about an increase in the repo rate.
"I think we can expect a further increase in the NBS repo rate, resulting from the higher yield on T-bills with longer maturities," Oto Mohnansky of Postova Banka said.
Dealers said the ministry accepted almost the entire amount of bids in order to finance incresing state budget deficit.
The budget deficit totalled 13.4 billion crowns as of September 30.
